item.title: Climbing Mount Fuji from Shizuoka: The Fujinomiya Trail — Guide
item.description: The Fujinomiya Trail is the main climbing route up Mount Fuji from the Shizuoka side, starting from the highest of the mountain’s four fifth-station trailheads at around 2,400 metres and offering the shortest, most direct path to the 3,776-metre summit, though its steeper, rockier terrain makes it more demanding step for step than the popular Yoshida route. Climbing is only permitted during the official summer season, roughly early July to early September, marked by the traditional trail-opening ceremonies, with mountain huts along the route and the summit crater and highest point, Kengamine, closest to this trail’s top.

item.title: Climbing Mount Fuji: The Yoshida Trail and Climbing Season — Guide
item.description: The Yoshida Trail is the most popular route to the 3,776-metre summit of Mount Fuji, starting from the Fuji Subaru Line 5th Station on Yamanashi’s northern side and offering the most mountain huts, first-aid stations and facilities of any Fuji route. Climbing is only permitted during a short official season each summer, roughly early July to early September, marked by the traditional Yamabiraki (mountain-opening) ceremony, with most climbers timing their ascent to reach the summit for the famous goraiko sunrise before descending the same day or after an overnight hut stay.
